# Changelog

Every release starts with its **Headline**: the single best feature that release brought (Boss, 2026-10-10). The sections under it keep the full record. The headline features still to come are listed in the [README](README.md#headline-features).

## [8.0.1990] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The uncharted black hole page test now says what the page answered when it fails.

### Fixed
- **`test_an_uncharted_black_hole_page_names_its_class` failed twice in loaded full gates and never alone (TEST.284).** The page was rendered without "Black Hole (Stellar)" and the failure printed nothing that said why. Run 150 times beside a six-worker load on the Bug Hunt lane it passed every time, so the cause is not found yet; the assertion now carries the status code, the headers and the start of the page, which tell a loading page (202), a redirect, a cached page of another row or a missing field apart on the next sighting.

## [8.0.1989] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** A benchmark suite test that needs the downloaded data now skips, saying so, on a machine without it.

### Fixed
- **`test_a_real_run_of_the_plan_writes_the_json_and_drops_its_databases` failed on a machine without the static downloads (TEST.285).** The suite starts the real plan step as a process, which refuses to run while a downloaded data file is missing (GEN.590, and Boss's missing-files rule), and the test then found exit status 1 where it expected 0. The suite times the real generator, so it takes no stand-in data; the test now looks for the missing files first and skips with their names, URLs and the setup command (`python3 -m planetgen.cli.datasets fetch`), and runs as before where the data is there.

## [8.0.1988] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The shape-report route's fuzz case, which ran past 900 s, now ends in under a minute.

### Fixed
- **`test_admin_pages_survive_hostile_query_when_logged_in[GET /admin/generate/shape-report]` ran past the 900 s test limit (TEST.275).** The fuzz sends many queries, and every one of them, junk keys or not, planned the default outline (`/admin/generate/shape-report` answers the line under the dials), which took 9 s to 10 s: the mean-system-mass age cache held 512 ages where one plan asks for about 23,000 (fixed by PERF.163), and the cell count of every shell was added up wedge by wedge again for each of the 1,532 shells, 1.8 million wedge calculations each time. `spherical.cells_in_band_range` is now cached like `shell_layout`, so the repeats of the same plan cost the rest of the plan only (about 2.4 s). The case alone takes 47 s, down from over 1,780 s.

## [8.0.1987] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The test that a dead worker never hangs a run no longer fails when the machine is merely slow.

### Fixed
- **`test_a_dead_worker_never_hangs_the_run` timed out once for two of its three attempts under heavy load (TEST.277).** It gave the whole run 60 s, and on a machine at load 14 to 20 starting the two worker processes, losing one and starting a fresh one took longer. It now waits for the run and gives up only when the run's record (the number of tasks in each state) stands still for 60 s, which is what a hung run does; a slow one keeps changing it.

## [8.0.1986] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The plan's crest and planned-share figures now come from the galaxy's own density and follow the Census dial.

### Fixed

- The plan's "Outline" line printed a crest of 11.5 times the one-star density where the model's own thin-disc crest was 8.76, and the same 11.5 with `--richness 1.0` where the model gives 4.37. The crest is now the number the outline walks on (`k_norm` x arm level x (1 + arm contrast) x the systems a sector holds at the real local density, `galaxy/plan_figures.py`), so it follows the galaxy's own system mass and the Census dial.
- The share of the stars in planned sectors (38 percent against the model's 59 for the same galaxy) was a table keyed on the thin crest alone and measured on the Milky Way's structure. It is now one integral of the built density over radius, height and azimuth, so a thick disc, bulge, nuclear disc or stellar halo of any size is in it. The table, the fixed 0.483 solar masses a system and the thin-disc surface-density shortcut are removed. The warning for a crest under 20 and the refusal of an empty outline are unchanged.

## [8.0.1985] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** A comet's coma is now drawn from the measured population of comets, with the carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide trading off and the carbon-chain-depleted flag set by the comet's family.

### Added
- **The comet volatile population (GEN.495).** `physics/comet_population.py` loads `physics/data/comet_population.json` and draws the ratios to water of CO, CO2, CH4, C2H6, NH3, HCN, CH3OH, H2CO and H2S. CO and CO2 come from a total (median 18 percent of water) and a CO share set by the dynamical class (Jupiter-family and Halley-type comets CO-poor, long-period ones balanced), redrawn while either leaves the observed range; the other species are truncated log-normals with the population's geometric mean and scatter; an interstellar comet takes the wider CO and CO2 ranges one measured object needs. The carbon-chain-depleted flag is the registered table `comet-carbon-chain`. Every number carries its source, label and state. No Solar System comet is a centre or a preset. Nothing stored reads the draw yet, so no draw changes.
- `DATA-LICENSE.md` lists the sources of the comet file, and the README points to it.

### Changed
- The design notes no longer describe a licence column in the element, gas and research tables; the licence is recorded in `DATA-LICENSE.md`.

generation-output: unchanged

## [8.0.1984] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The collision number of an object ID now follows the sectors' addresses, so two sectors that share an ID get the same names whichever one saved first.

### Changed
- **The object-ID collision number is keyed on the lower address (GEN.307).** Objects named by their 76-bit position ID (rogue planets, black holes, neutron stars, nebulae, supernova remnants, quasars, comets, asteroid fields) that share an ID take the collision numbers 0, 1, 2 ... in the order of their sectors' addresses, and in one sector in the order they were generated. `store._claim_object_ids` took the next free number, so when two sectors held objects with one ID the sector that saved first kept number 0. It now gets the sector's address (`save_sector` passes it): when a stored object of a higher address holds a number the new object outranks, the stored object moves up to the next number (`_rank_chain`). An object saved on its own, with no sector address, ranks after every sector, as it did. Every quasar shares the galactic centre's ID, so the quasars of a galaxy are the case this settles.
- `tests/test_object_id.py` saves three sectors with one shared ID in three orders into three databases and finds the same numbers 0, 1, 2 by address in each.

generation-output: changed

## [8.0.1983] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The saturation-pressure function now covers liquids as well as ices, up to the critical point.

### Changed
- **The liquid branch of the saturation-pressure function (GEN.452).** `physics/saturation.py` now answers above the triple point too, with the Wagner fits to the NIST saturation tables for hydrogen, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, nitrogen, oxygen, water, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, methane, ethylene, ethane, methanol, ammonia, hydrogen sulphide, sulphur dioxide and benzene and a correlation for hydrogen cyanide; hydrogen's solid comes from its triple point. Each answer says whether the condensate is solid or liquid, and above the critical temperature it says there is no saturation. At the triple point the two branches meet within a few percent (benzene 7), which is documented, not smoothed. Nothing reads the function yet, so no generated value changes.

## [8.0.1982] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The atmosphere recipes are now 104 gated rows in 16 tables, each with its source and its source state, ready for the generator to draw from.

### Added
- **The atmosphere possibility tables (GEN.478).** `physics/atmosphere_recipes.py` loads `physics/data/atmosphere_recipes.json`: the mantle redox, the delivered volatiles, the outgassed and retained regimes, the sub-Neptune envelope, the giants, brown dwarfs, hot Jupiters, lava worlds, frost and evolved atmospheres, comets, white-dwarf and pulsar planets, trace gases, clouds and hazes, ground radioisotopes and the host star's UV regime. Each row has a class gate, a weight that may depend on the mass, temperature, pressure, redox, insolation, the host and the formation distance over the snow line, the source of the weight with its verification label, and a source state. The 43 rows with no sourced weight are listed as open with their research item (GEN.480 to GEN.494) and draw a seeded value inside a physical bracket, never a fixed number. The tables register as `atmosphere-a` to `atmosphere-p`, and a draw of any table or of all of them in order is the same at any worker count. Nothing reads them yet, so no draw changes.
- **`Condition.one_of`** in the possibility-table loader: a gate on a quantity that may be any of several values.

### Changed
- The giants' carbon-to-oxygen recipe has an explicit core and tail (the part-05 recipe put 13.9 percent above 0.8), the atmosphere shoreline follows the published logistic and not the constants fitted to 13 Solar System bodies, and the redox of small bodies and white-dwarf debris follows the 22 measured white dwarfs.

## [8.0.1981] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The pressure at which any common gas turns to frost can be looked up from one place, with a note on how far to trust it.

### Changed
- **One saturation-pressure function (GEN.470).** The new `physics/saturation.py` and `physics/data/saturation_pressure.json` give the pressure at which the vapour and the solid are in balance, in pascals, for neon, nitrogen, carbon monoxide, argon, oxygen, methane, krypton, xenon, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, hydrogen sulphide, carbon dioxide, ammonia, sulphur dioxide, hydrogen cyanide, methanol, benzene and water. The first eighteen use the Fray and Schmitt 2009 polynomials as quoted in a later paper's table, water uses the Feistel and Wagner 2007 form (76.03 Pa at 250 K, 611.657 Pa at the triple point). Each answer carries a status: below 50 K it is marked `cold-unverified`, above the triple point `above-triple` (there is no liquid branch yet), and under a polynomial's turning point `below-fit`. Where a species has more than one fit the switch temperature is derived, not read from the paper, and is labelled a stand-in. Nothing reads the function yet (GEN.452 does), so no generated value changes.

generation-output: unchanged

## [8.0.1980] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The cache warm-up, the tile prefetch and the database check no longer wait behind a whole generation stage, because they have a queue and workers of their own.

### Changed
- **A maintenance lane.** The units of the cache warm-up and the database check, and the tile prefetch and rebuild jobs, now run on `planetgen-maintenance`, not on the generation queue. While a generation run is live that lane has `queue.maintenance_workers` workers (1 by default), taken out of the worker count: a generation worker finishes its unit and leaves when the lane needs its place, so the host's total does not grow, and the generation workers are back to the full count once the upkeep has drained. With no generation run live the lane may use the whole count (the warm-up and the check used to be held to one worker).
- **The tile prefetch works during a generation run.** Its queue limit (`tile_cache.prefetch_max_queued`) used to be checked against the whole generation queue, which a stage fills with thousands of units, so no tile was prefetched while a run was going; it now counts the upkeep queue only.

## [8.0.1979] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The photolysis lifetime of a molecule can be worked out for its star and its distance, species by species.

### Changed
- **The photolysis lifetime table (GEN.496).** The new `physics/photolysis.py` and `physics/data/photolysis_lifetimes.json` hold, for H2O, CO, CO2, CH4, C2H6, NH3, HCN, CH3OH, CH2O, H2S and N2, the lifetime at 1 AU from the quiet Sun, the range the sources give, the active-Sun factor where one was read (H2O 1.68, CO2 2.35, NH3 1.075) and the rate ratio around a 4000 K and a 10000 K star to the Sun's at equal ultraviolet flux. The rate follows the flux and, species by species, the star's spectrum: around a 4000 K star CO photolyses 3.5e-4 as fast as around the Sun and N2 2.9e-5, while NH3 hardly changes, so one scalar for "stellar UV" would be wrong by orders of magnitude. NH3 is the quiet-Sun 6.7e3 s, not the 5.6e3 s mean of quiet and active Sun. Stars outside 4000 to 10000 K take the end template and are flagged; shielding is not included. Nothing is stored and no generated value changes.

generation-output: unchanged

## [8.0.1978] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The generator now has one oxygen-fugacity scale, so a delta-IW means the same thing everywhere.

### Changed
- **One oxygen-fugacity scale (GEN.498).** The new `physics/oxygen_fugacity.py` fixes the reference as the Hirschmann 2021 iron-wustite buffer; every stored delta-IW, the mantle redox of a planet included, is on it. It converts the Frost 1991 buffers (QFM stands 3.1 to 3.6 above IW at 1 bar from 2200 to 1500 K) and the Sossi 2020 scale (his IW+0.5 for Earth is +0.0 on the reference) to it, gives the CO2/CO and H2O/H2 gas ratios at any delta-IW from the NASA Glenn fits of the five gases (CO2 equals CO at IW+1.37 and H2O equals H2 at IW-0.06 at 2173 K), and Sossi's melt Fe3+ law both ways. The reference fit's coefficients, the NASA Glenn fits and Sossi's law were checked against the papers; the Frost FMQ and NNO constants stay labelled stand-ins in the module's source rows. No stored value changes.

## [8.0.1976] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** One shared table now holds every material a body can be made of, with its density, phase points and equation-of-state constants and the source of each number.

### Added
- **The shared materials table (GEN.427).** `physics/materials.py` loads `physics/data/materials.json`: 158 rows, from part E's materials table, part B's SLB 2024 mantle phases and iron rows, part C's ice phases and the numbers read from Seager et al. 2007 (Tables 1 to 3), the Handbook of Mineralogy and PubChem. Every number carries its source and a read, computed, second-hand or not-reached code; a value with no source is empty, and part E's recalled cells are dropped. Each row has a class gate (`any`, or `planetary` for the high-pressure phases and the envelopes), a source and a verification state, and the rows are registered as the one shared `materials` table that other tables' fractions refer to. The 84 asteroid components, the field families, the comet list and the planet class composition texts all resolve to rows, and a test fails when one does not. Nothing reads it yet, so no draw changes.

### Changed
- **The licence is no longer a column.** The gas, element, isotope and decay-series files, the possibility-table row format, the dataset catalogue and the new materials table lose their licence field (Boss, 2026-10-22); the licence and source notes are in `DATA-LICENSE.md` in the repository root.

## [8.0.1975] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** One canonical encoder, nine significant digits, now writes every galaxy fingerprint, so a last-place difference in a float no longer shows as a different galaxy.

### Changed
- **The canonical fingerprint encoder (GEN.304).** `planetgen/util/fingerprint_encoding.py` writes any tree of dictionaries, lists, strings, integers, floats, decimals and bytes as one text: keys sorted, lists in generation order, floats as `format(x, ".8e")` (nine significant digits, -0.0 as 0.0, NaN and the infinities named), integers exact (hexadecimal above 2^53), strings quoted with every non-ASCII character escaped (no Unicode normalisation), and a `pgfp1` format tag hashed into every digest. Each value has a full digest, a structural digest (every float written `~`) and a float digest (the float tokens alone), so a comparison says whether the shape or a number changed. The same value gives the same digest on Python 3.12 and 3.13.
- `db/fingerprint.py` hashes through it: a row is a value, a sector's digest is over its rows in canonical order (a row's last-place float noise no longer changes the digest), `sector_sections` gives the three digests of a sector's named sections (`SECTIONS`: sector, system, star, planet, moon, belt, comet, phenomenon, population, plan), and `region_fingerprint(plain_names=True)` compares names without their collision decoration until GEN.57. Every digest printed by `planetgen fingerprint` changes once, with the format.
- The GEN.39 stand-in `tests/galaxy_fingerprint.py` is deleted; `tests/test_parallel_generation.py` compares the real fingerprint, and a failure names the sectors that differ. Its value tests moved to `tests/test_fingerprint_encoding.py`.

## [8.0.1972] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** The test workers no longer meet on the machine's one Redis database, which failed five tests of a full run.

### Fixed
- **Five tests failed in one full run because another worker's job was running (TEST.280).** `test_update_guard.py::test_the_command_begins_ends_and_reports`, three tests of `test_update_database_step.py` and `test_work_units.py::test_the_skeleton_is_one_unit...` start `planetgen` processes (or ask the update guard) on the machine's Redis with the default key prefix, which holds the one live-run lock and the `planetgen-bulk` queue. A real worker or run another xdist worker had started at that moment made them answer "work is running" and refuse. TEST.266 gave one test a database of its own; every worker now runs all its tests, and the processes they start, on the Redis database numbered after it, empty when the session starts and when it ends, so no worker sees another's runs or workers. `tests/private_redis.py` loses its fixture (the one test that took it needs nothing), the worker database reset forgets the stored counts in that database, and `PLANETGEN_TEST_REDIS_URL` still names the server whose database 0 `scripts/test.py` cleans.

## [8.0.1970] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** `planetgen link`, `backfill` and `settle` run the last stages of a galaxy run on their own.

### Changed
- **Three stages of `galaxy` are commands (PERF.123, first slice).** `planetgen link --since TIME` links the sectors saved since `TIME` to their neighbours, `planetgen backfill --since TIME` draws the bright stars out from them, and `planetgen settle --since TIME` saves their paths and those of the sectors around them. Each is one run on the work queue and does nothing when no sector was saved since `TIME`. A `galaxy` run now says its start time on the database's clock, the value these commands take. `galaxy` itself is unchanged for now.

## [8.0.1969] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** `planetgen sector` and `planetgen system` run through the work queue like every other generation command, so they show on the Queue page and take their turn.

### Changed
- **`sector` and `system` are runs of one command (PERF.119, first slice).** Each builds its step list from what was asked and hands it to the wrapper: the sectors of a `sector` run are cut into units that workers generate and save (each sector draws from its own seed, so a run gives the same sectors at any worker count), and a `system` run is one unit. A `system --output` run saves nothing, so it is a maintenance run and does not hold up generation. The old in-process pool for these two commands is gone; both now need Redis, as the other generation commands do.

## [8.0.1967] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** Drawing a system's content again keeps the ID of every star, planet, moon, belt and comet that keeps its place.

### Changed
- **A body's ID follows its slot, not its row (DB.75).** `replace_star_system_content` (the regenerate of `PATCH /api/systems/<id>`) used to delete a system's bodies and number the new ones from the system's counter, so every body got a new ID and a planet's public URL died with the redraw. A body now has a slot: a star's is its role, a planet's or belt's is the star it orbits and its place in that star's orbit list, a moon's is its planet's slot and its place among that planet's moons, a comet's is its star and its rank. The new body of a slot that the old content held takes that body's ID; a slot that is new takes the system's next body number; a slot that is gone leaves its number used for good (the counter is brought past every old body before the delete). Editing a system in place (`save_system_edits`) already kept every ID.
- `tests/test_stable_body_ids.py` redraws a system with fewer, then more, orbits and checks that every slot present before and after keeps its number, that a new slot takes a number no earlier body held, and that a fresh system still numbers its bodies 1, 2, 3 in the order it always did.

## [8.0.1966] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** A star's colour can be worked out from its temperature, the first part of the photometry library.

### Changed
- **Blackbody colour of a star (GEN.416).** The new `physics/photometry.py` takes a spectrum to a colour: the CIE 1931 curves (the Wyman, Sloan and Shirley fit), linear sRGB (D65) with the brightest channel 1, the sRGB curve, the 8-bit colour and the hex. `star_colour(temperature_k)` gives a star's colour: a Planck spectrum from 4500 K up, and for cooler stars the BT-Settl offset from the blackbody's chromaticity with a seeded spread the caller draws. It matches the table of the gas-optics design to 0.001 in chromaticity from 3000 K up. Nothing is stored and no generated value changes; the atmosphere colour work (GEN.418, GEN.419) and the view from a planet (VIEW.11) build on it.

generation-output: unchanged

## [8.0.1965] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** A short edit or estimate no longer waits behind a long neighbourhood job, because short and long jobs now have workers of their own.

### Changed
- **Short jobs have a reserved worker.** The workers for edits, estimates, wiki uploads and slow page answers (`queue.interactive_workers`, 1 by default) are no longer counted in the generation worker count, so a run on every core leaves them be, and they run at a higher priority (nice 5) than the generation workers (nice 10).
- **Long jobs have a lane of their own.** An API job expected to take longer than `queue.long_job_seconds` (60 by default), such as a neighbourhood or a large settle, goes to the `planetgen-long` queue and its `queue.long_workers` workers (1 by default), so it can never hold the worker kept for short jobs. A job with no estimate counts as short.
- **Pause and Resume on the Queue page now reach the workers.** Pause is a flag in Redis (`planetgen:queue:paused`): the workers of a run's units and of the maintenance work take no new job while it is set, a unit already running finishes, Resume releases them, and the two API lanes are never held. It no longer uses the work lease. `planetgen.cli.reset_jobs` clears the flag.
- **A run no longer fails with "run X is running" when another generation run holds the machine.** A generation run (a Generate stage, a one-sector regenerate or a neighbourhood from the API) waits in line, first come first served, for up to `queue.wait_minutes` (60 by default; 0 does not wait), then fails naming the run it waited for. A waiting Generate job's bar and a waiting API job's status (`waiting` in `GET /api/jobs/<id>`) read "Waiting at position 1 for run ...". A maintenance run or a database check still gets "busy" as before.
- The four new settings (`queue.interactive_workers`, `queue.long_workers`, `queue.long_job_seconds`, `queue.wait_minutes`) are on the settings page under "Speed and disk".

## [8.0.1964] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** A run can be told to go ahead without a missing data file, and a refusal now names every file to download.

### Changed
- **`--disregard-missing-data` (GEN.599).** A bulk run still refuses to start while a downloaded data file is missing, but the refusal now names each dataset, why, every file to download with its URL and the setup command. Told to disregard missing data (the option on the command line, the "Disregard missing data files" box on the Generate page, `disregard_missing_data` in the neighbourhood request), the run starts, says which datasets are missing and what stands in for each, and hands the option to every worker. The fallbacks: no main-sequence values for a star, the zero-temperature Chandrasekhar radius for a white dwarf, and the Chamel and Haensel 2008 outer crust for a neutron star; each is an open item on the star and a stand-in in the relation list. `datasets status --disregard-missing-data` reports the same and exits 0 for a dataset that has a fallback.

generation-output: unchanged

## [8.0.1963] - 2026-10-23

**Headline:** `planetgen benchmark --suite` times every generation step on a galaxy of a chosen size, and the first round of fixes it found makes the massive-star scatter at the default size take minutes, not hours.

### Added
- **`planetgen benchmark --suite`** (PERF.146). Builds a scratch galaxy of a chosen size (`tiny`, `small`, `medium`, `large`), runs each generation step as its own measured command (wall time, machine CPU, peak memory, database questions and rows, time per star or cell, the stages the step reports) and prints a table ranked by share of the whole run; `--repeats` gives the run-to-run spread, `--steps` picks steps, `--step-timeout` stops a step that runs away and records it as not finished, `--output` writes the JSON. See `docs/cli.md`.
- **`docs/design/generation-performance.md`**: the measured cost of every step, a ranked list of what to speed up next, and the py-spy recipe the profiles were taken with.

### Changed
- **A queue worker builds the galaxy's component field and sampling tables once, before it forks a job, not once per unit.** The scatter units were each rebuilding the field from about 22,000 clusters and satellites; the massive-star scatter at the default size took over two hours and now takes about three minutes. The drawn values are unchanged.
- **The mean system mass at an age is about four times faster** (the remnant states and turn-off mass are worked out once per call, and the lifetime terms once per metallicity), with the same numbers.
- **The scatter's band tiers are looked up together** (one pass over the density arrays for all the places a component's stars land in) instead of one band at a time, bit for bit the same tiers; the supervisor's tier lookup for marked cells is vectorised the same way.

## [8.0.1958] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The physical laws the generator writes by hand about fifty times are now declared once in `physics/relations.py`, each with a fast SI kernel and a Quantity form, and a dimension test in the math check.

### Added
- **`physics/relations.py`** (GEN.586): 21 named laws (Schwarzschild radius, surface gravity, escape, circular and
  vis-viva speeds, Kepler's third law and mean motion, break-up rate, rotation period and rate, Hill radius, Roche
  limit, sphere volume, mean density and radius, black-body luminosity and effective temperature, inverse-square flux,
  equilibrium temperature, mass flow). Each is one function: `relations.surface_gravity(mass_kg, radius_m)` takes
  plain SI floats and is the kernel; `relations.quantities.surface_gravity(mass_quantity, radius_quantity)` runs the
  same formula on `Quantity` values and answers a `Quantity` of the declared kind, bit for bit the kernel's answer.
  Constants come from the registry's table (`c.G`), never typed. The vector laws (obliquity, galactic orbit) are left
  to GEN.584.
- **A dimension test**: each formula is run once on probe objects that carry a dimension, and the answer must have its
  declared kind's dimension; the new `relations_have_their_dimension` invariant in the math check runs it before
  anything else, so a missing square, a missing constant, a wrong root or a length added to a mass fails the suite.
- Kinds area and volume (m², km², cm², m³, km³, cm³, liters) in the unit registry.
- Nothing is replaced yet: GEN.587 moves the hand-written sites onto the laws, file group by file group, wherever the
  golden set stays bit-identical.

## [8.0.1957] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The unit registry now has unit systems, and a physical constant's number in AU, year and solar mass is worked out from its dimension.

### Added
- **Unit systems** (GEN.585): `unit_registry.UnitSystem` is four registry units (length, mass, time, temperature);
  `si` and `au-yr-msun` are declared. `constant_in("G", "au-yr-msun")` (also c, sigma, k_B, hbar), `in_system` and
  `system_factor` work a number out from its dimension and the system's base units, so a typed shortcut such as 4 pi
  squared can be generated and checked. The computed G for the solar mass in the Julian year is 39.4769, 3.8e-5 below
  the typed 39.4784 of `kepler.AU3_PER_YR2_PER_SOLAR_MASS` (the Gaussian year's); the difference is stated in the
  module header and pinned by a test, and GEN.587's sweep decides which stands.
- Kinds force and mass flow, with newtons, dynes, kg/s, g/s and solar and Earth masses per year; a test that every kind
  has a five-integer dimension and that the derived kinds the code uses have theirs.
- The column registry (DB.76) lost its local `km3`: the unit registry now holds it with the area and volume kinds.

## [8.0.1949] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** Every length column now declares its role, its frame and how far it must hold, and the table says what size of body each table can place.

### Changed
- **The precision table (`db/precision.py`).** The 182 length columns of the column registry each declare a role (`position`, `separation`, `size`, `relative` or `derived`); a position or separation also declares its frame (galaxy, sector or system) and a reach: the bound-orbit limit of 10,000 AU, the Hill-sphere ceiling a comet's closed orbit reaches, the half-diagonal of a sector cell, or the largest Edge the galaxy dials allow. From the spacing of a double in the column's unit at that reach, `floor_body_m(table)` gives the smallest body the table places to a tenth of its size: 2.4 m for planets, moons and belts (km column inside 10,000 AU), 2.7 m for stars (AU column), 620 m for comets at the stability ceiling, and about 9,000 km for a body stored free in a galaxy frame at the largest Edge (33 m at 8 kpc). Nothing in the data moves.
- `tests/test_precision.py` fails when a length column has no declaration, when a position's frame is not its table's, when planets or moons cannot place a 10 m body, when a reach no longer matches its source (the Hill sphere, the sector edge, the Edge dial's maximum), and when a table's floor moves from the documented one. The figures and the way out for a wanderer are in `docs/design/unified-unit-quantity.md`, section 6.1.

## [8.0.1945] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The galaxy's density is now the sum of named components, with each component's mass in solar masses, and the stored family and component numbers are read back.

### Changed
- **The density model is one list of components (GEN.379).** `relative_density`, `population_densities` and the two array forms take each component's value from one place (`galaxy.density.component_values` for a point, `component_arrays` for arrays of points): the thin disk with its arms, the thick disk, the bulge or bar, the stellar halo and the nuclear cluster and disc. A component with amplitude 0 is exactly 0. Every density is the same to the last digit as before (a fixture of six shapes at 24 points checks it) and the array forms are as fast.
- **`component_masses(shape)` now returns each component's mass in solar masses**, by name, from the closed forms; the six sum to the galaxy's stellar mass. The numerical integral it used to be is `integrated_masses`, which the math check and the tests use.
- **The stored family and component numbers are read and written (DB.66).** `get_galaxy_shape` puts `family`, the bar's presence, axis ratios and angle, the thick disk's amplitude, the spheroid's numbers and the clump share into `GalaxyShape`; a NULL bar or thick disk number means the structure draw's own value, a number pins it. `save_galaxy_shape` writes them, replacing what an earlier plan stored. A stored spheroid amplitude above 0 is refused until the spheroid component is built.

- **One admin shell.** The tab row is replaced by a rail of six destinations (Overview, Generate, Settings, Jobs, Data, Account), a search box and a Compact switch (compact by default, remembered in this browser). ## [8.0.1924] - 2026-10-22

The five modes and three center choices of the old form are gone from the page; the command each builds is unchanged, and a test holds it.

## [8.0.1922] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The unit ladders take every factor from the unit registry, and a `Quantity` can be shown on the site's ladders directly.

## [8.0.1921] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** A point in space now takes its length unit by registry key and states no unit factor of its own.

### Changed
- **`SpatialPosition3D` takes `length_unit` ("m", "au", "ly", "pc"), a length key of the unit registry, instead of
  `length_unit_m`** (GEN.573). The factor comes from `unit_registry`; a key that is no length unit is refused. The point
  class loses its own `SPEED_OF_LIGHT_MS` (it reads `constants.SPEED_OF_LIGHT_M_S`), the bare 1000 between m/s and km/s
  (the registry's km/s factor, here and in `MassObject`), and `mu_of` and `mass_of` (a mass and its `mu` are the
  registry's declared "mass-mu" relation). Every stored and drawn value is bit-identical.

## [8.0.1920] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** A number with a unit is now one `Quantity` object that keeps what it was given and answers in every other unit of its kind.

### Added
- **`planetgen.physics.quantity.Quantity`** (GEN.569). `Quantity("power", 3.828e26, "W")` keeps the number and unit as
  given and never converts them; `.kW`, `.Lsun` and `.as_("erg_s")` give every other unit of its kind, worked out from
  the truth on first read and kept, and `set` drops them so every form is in step. A relation of the registry answers
  a quantity of another kind (`related`: a mass's gravitational parameter, a radius's diameter, a period's frequency).
  A value is checked finite and inside its kind's bounds when made or set, and a unit of another kind is refused by
  name. `to_dict` gives `{kind, value, unit}`. It is for the edges; the generator's kernels stay on plain floats.

### Changed
- `unit_registry.convert` multiplies or divides by the power of ten itself when two units' factors are a power of ten
  apart (`unit_registry.scale`): 1.5 km is exactly 1500.0 m, where the two-step product rounded twice for about a
  third of all values.

## [8.0.1919] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** A Reed-Solomon codec in the standard library lets the sector parity file rebuild lost data exactly.

### Added
- **`planetgen.util.rscodec`, a GF(256) Reed-Solomon erasure code with no new dependency (DB.43).** `RS(k, m)` makes
  `m` parity blocks from `k` data blocks (`encode`), gives the data back from any `k` of the `k + m` blocks
  (`decode`), and makes the new parity when one member changes from its old and new bytes (`update`). The first
  parity block is the plain XOR of the data. Members of unequal length work through zero padding. Nothing reads it
  yet: the parity file (DB.46) and the repair command (DB.47) stand on it.

- **`planetgen plan` draws the skeleton and nothing else (PERF.121).** The scatters moved to a new `planetgen scatter` that takes exactly one of `--mass`, `--luminosity`, `--phenomena`, `--nebula-field` or `--band --down-to N`, with only that kind's options (`--phenomenon-min-mass` for the mass pass, `--bright-star-min-luminosity` for both star passes, `--compact-min-mass` for the phenomena). ## [8.0.1915] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** A built star system now keeps its tree of orbits in the database, and the system scene places its stars from that tree.

### Added
- **The orbit tree is stored and loaded with the system (GEN.311).** `insert_star_system` writes the system's tree into `orbit_nodes`: a generated binary is one node made from the pair it was generated with (separation, eccentricity, plane, phase held at the database's orbit epoch, period, mass), and a system that carries its own tree has it stored as it is. `load_star_system` and the JSON form (`StarSystem.to_dict`, serialization version 4) bring it back as `StarSystem.orbit_nodes`. ## [8.0.1913] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** Every unit the project uses is now one row in a single registry, with its kind, exact factor, symbol and allowed range.

### Added
- **`planetgen.physics.unit_registry`** (GEN.568). One row per unit: an ASCII key, a display symbol, a name, the kind it
  measures, the factor to the kind's SI base unit and the offset of its zero (only the temperature scales have one).
  Kinds carry a five-exponent dimension and the values they allow (a mass, duration, power or pressure is at least 0, a
  speed is below c, everything is finite). A temperature difference is its own kind, so 10 K warmer is 10 degrees
  Celsius warmer. Compound units (km/s, AU/yr, pc/Myr) are declared by their parts and tested against them. Relations
  between kinds are data: a mass and its gravitational parameter, a radius and its diameter, a period and its
  frequency, a rotation period and its angular rate. Angular rate and angular momentum are new kinds.
- Tests hold every factor against its definition written out in full, each ladder rung of `util/ladders.py` against a
  registry unit of the same factor, round trips, and the bounds. No existing file changes: the duplicate names in
  `constants.py` stay until GEN.571 sweeps them.

## [8.0.1912] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** What a collision does is one tested function: the outcome table for rocky bodies, giants, brown dwarfs and stars.

### Added
- **`physics/collision_outcome.py`** (GEN.345): `resolve(a, b, impact_parameter_m, window_start_unix)` turns two bodies that have come within `R1 + R2` into an `Outcome`, the rows of the section 5.1 table of `docs/design/collisions-and-mergers.md`: merger, graze-and-merge, hit-and-run, partial erosion and disruption for two rocky bodies (from the catastrophic energy of Leinhardt and Stewart and the lens a grazing pass overlaps), absorption by a giant or star, tidal disruption near a compact remnant, giant mergers that lose a little gas and then pass the deuterium and hydrogen fusion lines (`hydrogen_burning_limit_sol(z)`, a new star flagged "merger remnant" with no planets), and stellar mergers. Pure: no database, no draw, the same outcome in either order of the pair; mass and momentum are conserved to 1e-12. Settings: `ALWAYS_DESTROY_TERRESTRIAL` (Boss's literal rule) and the speed, energy and share cut-offs in `tuning.py`.

## [8.0.1911] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The orbital update can find every mass within the galaxy's largest Hill radius of an object, the first step of changing a path by gravity.

### Added
- **The influence-set search** (`galaxy/influence.py`, GEN.341). `largest_hill_radius_pc` is the one search radius for the whole galaxy: the largest galactic Hill radius over each sector's heaviest mass, from the galaxy's own mass inside the object's radius (GEN.370), with the central black hole skipped (the smooth potential holds it). `influence_set` reads the sectors that can hold part of that sphere (found by sector bounds, the radius widened by the cells' reach of 1.3 edges, so no ring-and-slot stencil and no cover lists), keeps the members within the radius, returns the 64 nearest one by one and folds the rest into one point mass per sector, in an order that does not depend on how the sectors were stored. It moves nothing and reads no database; the caller gives `read_sector(address)`.
  - `tests/test_influence.py` checks it against numpy brute force and a `cKDTree` at the core, a ring face, mid radius, the rim, both sides of the slot-0 seam and the top and bottom layers (radii 2, 6, 20 and 60 pc; no mismatch), shows that dropping the reach margin misses neighbours, checks that every object whose own Hill sphere holds the target is in the set with injected heavy objects, and checks the cap (the nearest 64 exact, the mass conserved, the pull within 5% of the full sum), the shuffled order, a lone rogue, a hierarchy given as one point and the refusals.

## [8.0.1910] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The orbital update has the pair closest-approach library its collision and encounter tests will use.

### Added
- **`physics/closest_approach.py`** (GEN.334): whether two paths come within `R` of each other in a window, and when. `sweep` is the closest-approach form (the miss distance as a vector first, then the entry time), exact where the swept-sphere form of the source document loses the miss distance once the start is far away; `Segment`, `linear_state_at` and `pair_window` give the pair-window rule (a body's update against the other's stored segment over `[max(e_X_prev, e_Y), e_X_now]`, positions differenced from sector-relative values); `window_cap` and `chunks` cut a long step at the galactic tide's curvature bound and one sector's crossing time (and 0.1 Myr); `first_hit` walks the chunks. No collision outcome or candidate search lives here (GEN.345, GEN.110, the broad phase).

## [8.0.1909] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The orbit stepper and the browser's orbit positions keep their digits over long times, and Python and JavaScript agree (GEN.140, GEN.374, GEN.144).

### Changed
- **Stumpff functions by series for `|z| < 1`** (GEN.140): `kepler.stumpff_c2_c3`, the compiled `state_kernel._stumpff` and `stumpff` in `orbitpositions.js` sum ten terms of the series below `|z| = 1` (it was `1e-3`), where the closed forms cancel and a hyperbolic `c3` was off by 4e-13. Body positions the universal step gives on the maps change in the thirteenth digit and below; nothing stored by a generate changes (the step runs on read, `physics/body_positions.py`).
- **Orbit phases reduce first** (GEN.374): `kepler.wrapped_turn_deg(elapsed, period)` is `360 fmod(elapsed, period) / period`, used for circular bodies and elliptical comets (`physics/body_positions.py`), the nodes of a multi-star system (`physics/system_tree.py`) and `wrappedTurnDeg` in `orbitpositions.js`; the plain ratio is off by about 1e-4 degrees for a 0.3 day period at 1e9 days. The JavaScript Kepler solver's tolerance is 1e-12 (it was 1e-10), as the Python one.

- **One named Sun radius, and the rotation-curve comment corrected** (GEN.144): `mathcheck.SUN_REFERENCE_RADIUS_PC` is the Gaia 8.128 kpc (it was 8.2 kpc), and the comment above `GALACTIC_ROTATION_FLAT_VELOCITY_KMS` says what the curve gives there (206 km/s, 242 Myr) and that it is a stand-in the potential replaces, instead of claiming the real Sun's values. The Milky Way plausibility tests (`test_sector_gen`, `test_star_matrix`) read that one radius.

### Added
- Tests (GEN.140, GEN.374): the Stumpff functions against exact rational arithmetic, the series-limit join, DOUBLE period and phase columns, radial (h = 0) motion, the wrapped turn against exact arithmetic, and Python and JavaScript agreeing on the Stumpff functions, the wrapped turn and the positions of every body at 3,000, 27,000 and 100,000 years. `docs/design/orbital-solvers-and-integrators.md` section 7 lists which guards are built and which wait on code not yet written.

## [8.0.1906] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The test that interrupts a parallel galaxy run no longer fails as "Busy" when another test worker has a run going.

### Fixed
- **`test_interrupting_a_parallel_galaxy_run_leaves_no_half_written_sector` failed under load with "run ... is running" (TEST.266).** The test starts `planetgen generate` as a process, which takes the machine's one live-run lock (`planetgen:run:active`) on the shared Redis server; a process cannot be given the key prefix the in-process tests get, so a second test worker running at the same time was refused. Reproduced by starting the test twice at once (before: one of the two failed Busy; after: both pass). Each worker now takes the Redis database numbered after it for the processes it starts (`tests/private_redis.py`).

## [8.0.1902] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** Every galaxy's Hill spheres use the mass the galaxy holds inside the object's own distance from the centre, not the whole halo's mass.

### Changed
- **A star's, binary's, compact object's and rogue's Hill sphere takes the galaxy's mass inside its own radius** (`galaxy/enclosed_mass.py`, GEN.370). The central mass was the mass chain's whole virial mass at every radius (`mass_chain.central_mass_kg`), but most of the halo lies outside a star's orbit, so the Hill spheres were several times too small (a drawn galaxy of 9.5e12 solar masses of halo and 9.0e10 of stars encloses 1.6e10 inside 1 kpc and 1.2e11 inside 8 kpc). The enclosed mass is the density model's stars (the smooth components integrated on a cylindrical grid, the arms averaged round each circle), the central black hole and the chain's own NFW dark halo (its halo mass less its stars, its virial radius and concentration). The gas is left out until GEN.338's potential gives the enclosed mass.
  - `Star.calculate_system_perimeter`, `BinaryStarProxy._calculate_system_perimeter_static` and the keep-out query (`db/query.py` `keep_out_radius`) read it at the object's own distance; `mass_chain.central_mass_kg`, `current_central_mass_kg` and `MassChain.halo_mass_kg` are gone.
  - A unit reads the galaxy's stored shape (`seeded(..., shape=...)`, bound by `run_galaxy`, `nebula_field` and `superbubble_field`), or the shape its seed draws with every lever on Auto (`shape_draw.default_shape`, what `plan` makes with no shape option). Dial-pinned masses (`GalaxyShape.masses`) reach the model, so a pinned Scale or Halo dial changes the Hill spheres.
  - A galaxy twice the size encloses less at one radius, and so has wider Hill spheres (`tests/test_enclosed_mass.py`).
  - **The placement fill is rechecked** (`docs/design/course-avoidance.md` section 4.1): the Hill spheres of a mean-mass system fill 0.3 to 0.9 of the volume over a disk's inner and middle radii (the old value never passed 0.03), and in a dense galaxy the placer now fits 60 to 70% of the requested systems of a 4 pc cell at 1 kpc and 35 to 45% at 3 kpc, where it fitted all of them; sparser galaxies are unchanged except 1 system in 16 at 3.7 kpc.
- The generator epoch is 48.
generation-output: changed

### Added
- `tests/test_enclosed_mass.py`: the mass grows with the radius and ends at the galaxy's whole mass, the black hole is most of the centre, the stars agree with a Monte Carlo of the density model within 6%, the dark halo follows NFW, a galaxy twice the size changes the Hill radius, and a star's and a pair's perimeter read the mass inside their own radius from the shape the unit is given.

## [8.0.1901] - 2026-10-22

## [8.0.1899] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The speed at which an ejected neutron star streams out of a galaxy now follows its natal kick and the galaxy's escape speed.

### Changed
- An ejected neutron star's far speed is what its kick leaves above the escape speed at its birth radius (`galaxy.natal_kick.ejecta_speeds_kms`), kept as 16 quantiles in the galaxy's structure (`Structure.neutron_star_ejecta_speeds_kms`), instead of a speed uniform from 300 to 500 km/s. For a galaxy of the Milky Way's structure the mean is 386 km/s; a deeper well or a slower kick gives slower ones, and a galaxy that ejects none has no ejecta population. The population's density and outer radius take the mean speed (`ejecta_field.mean_speed_kms`); ejected black holes keep the 300 to 500 km/s range, a stand-in until they have a kick model. `docs/design/natal-kick.md` records the model.

## [8.0.1893] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** A galaxy's number of systems follows from a mean system mass worked out from the generator's own star mix, not a recalled 0.4 solar masses.

### Changed
- **The mean mass of a system is derived (`generation/system_mass.py`, `galaxy/system_mass.py`, `density.mean_system_mass_solar`).** `tuning.MEAN_SYSTEM_MASS_SOLAR` (0.4, "recalled, within a factor of 1.5") is gone. For stars formed at one age the mean is the placed star's present mass from the initial mass function (its birth mass until its last giant phase ends, then its white dwarf, neutron star or black hole) plus the other stars of its system: the `star-count` table's mean number by the placed star's class with the 8 to 12 tail (`multistar.expected_star_count`) times the mean present mass of a star born with 0.1 to 1 of the primary's mass. A population's mean averages the ages by its star formation (the disk's history; the other windows uniformly), and a galaxy's or cell's averages the populations by their systems. The reference galaxy comes out at 0.483 solar masses a system (young 0.71, intermediate 0.54, old 0.48, bulge 0.47, halo 0.47: a placed star of 0.35 and 1.42 stars a system), so it holds 1.03e11 systems where the constant gave 1.25e11, and the density at the reference radius is 0.62 of the pinned local density (0.750 after GEN.544).
  - `galaxy.density.build_galaxy_shape` divides the stellar mass by it; `galaxy.resolution` (the mass of a cell's unresolved systems), `generation.place_terms.from_profile` (a place's mass density) and the math check read the cell's or galaxy's own mean.
  - The initial mass function integrals and the cohort moments moved from `generation/place_terms.py` to `generation/system_mass.py`; the perturber mass is unchanged. The empty-cell fallback of `mass_weighted_perturber_mass_solar` is the disk's mean system mass.
  - `galaxy.disk_history.history_of` ignores `k_norm`, so the history computed while the density is normalized is the one every later read of the shape uses.
  - `multistar.MAX_MEMBERS`, `multistar.COMPANION_MASS_FRACTION` and `multistar.expected_star_count` name what `draw_member_tree` already did.
  - `CLUSTER_MEAN_SYSTEM_MASS_SOL` (the clusters' and satellites' 0.4) is a separate constant and stays.
- The generator epoch is 46.

### Added
- `tests/test_gen_system_mass.py`: the expected star count against the generator's own draw, the placed star's mean against a seeded initial mass function draw, the other stars against real member trees, and the whole against seeded systems at three ages.

## [8.0.1891] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** Every block of the Galaxy Map's ladder now knows how much of it is nebula, before any sector in it is generated.

### Added
- **Nebula totals per block (MAP.172, schema v116).** For each of the five levels above a sector, `nebula_block_stats` holds the nebulae in a block (counted in the block that holds the centre): their number, volume, volume-weighted centroid, the bounding radius around it, the volume of each family and the class with the most volume. Its `cover` is the share of the block inside a nebula: each cloud's volume is split among the blocks it reaches (so a cloud wider than a block shades every block it touches), the pieces add up exactly through the ladder, and the summed volume becomes a share the way randomly placed clouds cover a volume (`1 - exp(-v / V)`, never above 1). A Monte Carlo test checks the stored cover against random points thrown at a block, at the 256 pc cells and up that the shading uses: it is within 5% (3.8% at the worst of nine blocks) with the field 11% full.
- The totals come from `nebula_field` and the stored nebulae that are not field clouds, so no sector has to exist. The migration fills them from what the galaxy holds, `planetgen plan` makes them with the nebula field, and `planetgen plan --fill-nebula-blocks` makes them again. A `galaxy` run adds the nebulae it stored once at its end, so its workers never queue on the same top-level blocks (`nebula_block_state` keeps the highest nebula id folded in).
- Nothing reads the totals yet: the map's colour choice, the region layer and the tile format are the next items of the design (docs/design/nebula-map-visibility.md, section 9).

## [8.0.1884] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The Admin menu on the sector, system and phenomenon pages now opens under its button instead of far above it, off the screen.

### Fixed
- **The Admin menu (and the Navigate menu) opened off the visible window (UX.145).** The action row is a size container (`container-type: inline-size`, UX.27), which also makes it the containing block of the menus inside it. The menus' placement (Shoelace's Floating UI reads `offsetParent`) did not know that and measured against the page, so a menu opened as far above its button as the row is from the top of the page: off the top of a short window, and detached from its button on any window. The row is now `position: relative`, so the offset parent and the containing block are the same element. A browser test opens the Admin menu on every page that has it, at a laptop, a small laptop, a tablet, a phone and a short window, in both themes, and checks that it hangs at its button, lies inside the window and that every entry can be reached.

## [8.0.1882] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** A zoom on the Galaxy Map no longer stalls the page walking every star for every tile that has not arrived.

### Changed
- **Carrying stars over to tiles still on the way (MAP.249).** While the tiles of a new zoom level arrive, the map keeps drawing the stars already on screen where the new tiles will be. For that it walked all the drawn stars once for each missing tile: about 250 tiles by 45,000 stars is 11 million box tests, 665 ms of main-thread time on the test machine, repeated on each fetch step of a zoom. It now places each star in its tile with arithmetic in one pass (6.5 ms for the same case) and carries the same stars.
- **A view known from its tiles (MAP.249).** Each time tiles arrived or the camera settled with every tile in hand, the map built a list of every star in the view (up to 45,000) and sorted and joined it, about 160 ms of main-thread time on each call, only to find the stars were the ones already drawn. It now compares the tiles themselves (`static/tileview.js`): a view whose tiles are the ones already drawn costs a pass over about 250 tile keys. Nothing a visitor sees changes; the page works the same with fewer pauses on a zoom.
- **Guards.** A test fails if a view asks for more than 220 tiles at any of eight camera distances from 30 to 100,000 parsecs, and a script test fails if signing a view of 250 tiles reads a star or takes over 5 ms.

**Headline:** The Structure dial sets how flat the disc is and how big and heavy the bulge is, as ratios that keep their meaning when the galaxy's size changes.

### Changed
- **The Structure dial (GEN.604).** `--flatness` (scale length over scale height, 3 to 20), `--bulge-share` (bulge-to-total mass, 0 to 0.9) and `--bulge-size` (bulge scale radius over the scale length, 0.02 to 1) are in the lever table and on the Generate page. ## [8.0.1875] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The Scale, Halo and Edge dials set a galaxy's mass and size, its halos and how far out it is planned, the plan remembers what was pinned, and a small galaxy is one disc plus a bulge.

### Changed
- **The Scale dial (GEN.603).** `--mass` (stellar mass, solar masses), `--compactness` (size in standard deviations from the size-mass law), `--disk-scale-length` and `--density` (the thin disc's central surface density) are in the lever table and on the Generate page. They are three views of two numbers: pin any two and the third is shown, pin all three and the plan is refused naming the density the other two imply. A pinned value replaces only its own draw, so the same seed at twice the mass keeps its size residual and its thick disc. With nothing pinned the galaxy is the one the seed drew before.
- **The plan stores what it was told (DB.81).** Migration 0114 adds `galaxy_shape.pinned_stellar_mass_solar` and the table `galaxy_shape_pins`. A loaded galaxy is drawn again at the stored mass (its structure, its mass chain, the tidal field every Hill sphere reads), `GET /api/galaxy/shape` carries `pins` and `pinned_stellar_mass_solar`, and the Generate page says which levers were pinned and that the rest were drawn.
- **No halo under about 4.6 million solar masses of stars.** A galaxy whose halo would weigh under 1e10 solar masses (`dials.HALO_MIN_HALO_MASS_SOLAR`, where the concentration and stellar-to-halo laws were fitted from) draws no halo mass, virial radius or concentration and runs no law that reads them: its tidal mass is its stars', its disc's gas inflow is constant and it has no stellar halo. Drawn galaxies (3e9 solar masses and up) are unchanged.
- **New limits.** Stellar mass 281 to 1.55e11 solar masses, scale length 28 to 8250 pc and scale height 4 to 1155 pc: half of Segue 1 (the length floor raised to 28 pc, one grid cell's reach) up to 1.5 times Andromeda (Boss, 10-21).
- **The Halo dial (GEN.606).** `--halo-ratio` (dark halo mass over stellar mass, 10 to 3000) and `--stellar-halo-share` (0.001 to 0.3) replace only their own draw; the plan prints the halo's mass, virial radius and concentration and warns when a pinned size or halo makes a disc the halo would not hold. A pin on a galaxy that has no such halo is refused, and the Generate page turns those fields off while the stellar mass typed is under the threshold, with the reason.
- **The Edge dial (GEN.605).** `--edge` takes a length with its unit, `12L` (3 to 20 scale lengths of the thin disc), `160pc`, `40kpc` or `0.1Mpc` (4 pc to the grid's 262 kpc reach) and stops the outline there; with none the outline ends where no sector clears the one-star density. `planetgen plan --max-shell` is retired with no shim (the benchmark's own option now passes `--edge`).
- **One disc plus a bulge under 3e8 solar masses of stars.** No thick disc, bar, stellar halo or nuclear cluster and disc (Boss, 10-21: the laws that draw them were fitted to bigger galaxies; at 281 solar masses the thick disc was 906 times the thin one). Drawn galaxies (3e9 and up) are unchanged.
- **Hard limits and warnings from the density report.** Scale length 28 to 8250 pc, scale height at least 4 pc, bulge radius at least 2 pc, a pitch angle at least 1 degree from flat, central surface density 0.03 to 1e5 solar masses per square parsec; a plan with pins whose outline would be empty is refused, and one whose disc crest is under 20 times the one-star density prints the share of its stars in planned sectors.
- **One arm contrast (GEN.611).** `--arm-density` and `--interarm-density` are retired with no shim for `--arm-contrast`, 0 to 1, default 0.4: the thin disc is `1 + contrast` of its mean on an arm crest and `1 - contrast` between arms. A new plan stores `arm_level` 1; `density.arm_terms` is removed.
- **Every dial range is in the registry (GEN.609).** `docs/design/gap-filling-plan.md` section 6.3a lists each lever's range, label (verified, derived, bracket, theory or placeholder) and source, written from the lever table, and a test fails when it goes stale. The ranges that were only recalled stay brackets or placeholders while network access is closed.
- **The neutron star ejected share follows a pinned mass (GEN.554).** `structure_draw.draw_neutron_star_unbound_share` takes the pinned stellar mass, and a galaxy under the halo threshold has the escape speed of its stars alone. Drawn galaxies keep their share.

## [8.0.1873] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** A star's fate as a neutron star or a black hole now depends on its initial mass in windows, and the neutron stars a galaxy ejects now follow from its escape speed, instead of two overlapping ranges and a drawn 20% to 40%.

### Changed
- A neutron star's or black hole's progenitor is drawn from the windows of initial mass where massive stars explode or fail (`physics/remnant_progenitors`): the verified islands at 23 to 25 and 35 to 45 solar masses (O'Connor and Ott 2011, Sukhbold et al. 2016), shrunk or widened to hold the failed share of the 8 to 150 solar mass stars, down to about 14.5 solar masses at the widest verified share. A black hole whose progenitor failed collapsed directly; the fixed 40 solar mass rule is gone.
- Remnant ages follow the new progenitors (`collapse_age_gy` moved to `physics/remnant_progenitors`). The perturber mass of the placement limits follows the failed share: 1.01 solar masses for the whole disk (1.44 before), so a wide pair near the Sun survives to about 1.6e4 AU (1.1e4 before). `docs/design/explosion-islands.md` records the model.
- The share of a galaxy's neutron stars its natal kicks eject is derived (`galaxy/natal_kick.py`): a Maxwellian kick of 265 km/s against the escape speed of the galaxy's halo and stars, averaged over the thin disc's birth radii, replacing the uniform 20% to 40% draw. A galaxy of the Milky Way's published masses ejects 27% (inside the old range, now a test target), the generator's median halo 16% and escape speed 539 km/s at 8.2 kpc; the galaxies the generator draws run from none to 74%, the small ones losing most. The black hole share cap is the Milky Way-like galaxy's for every galaxy, so a galaxy that ejects most of its neutron stars is not left with no stellar black holes. At the middle draw a standalone sector rolls 4.66e-3 neutron stars per star (Boss's 4.0e-3 research density is a test target, 16% under) and 8.6e-4 black holes. `docs/design/natal-kick.md` records the model.

### Fixed
- **A rocky planet of a wide pair could have a light swing above 1 (GEN.597).** When the planet's star is the dim one of the pair (a white dwarf or a brown dwarf beside a bright star) the companion's swing over the mean total light passed 1 (1.6 to 2.6 in seeds 36 and 106 of the test's sweep). `insolation.companion_swing` is now capped at 1, as the circumbinary swing is. The insolation test sweeps 240 seeds instead of 60.

## [8.0.1872] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** A Generate run no longer sits for hours on one unit drawing a Magellanic Cloud: a large satellite or cluster is drawn in slices that the workers share, and every unit of components reports its progress.

### Fixed
- **A Generate run stalled for hours on its components (the star scatter's last unit, then the phenomena's).** All the globular clusters, open clusters and satellite galaxies were one unit, drawn by one worker one star after another. With a low luminosity floor the Large Magellanic Cloud alone holds about a million stars, so that unit was nearly all of the stage's work, took more than an hour on a single worker while the other workers stood idle, and reported nothing until it ended, so the bar stuck near the start with an estimate of 30 hours. The components are now cut into tasks by their expected stars (or phenomena) alone, the same at any worker count: a component with more than 25,000 expected stars (1,000,000 expected phenomena) is cut into slices, one unit each, and the smaller ones are bundled in order up to that size. The units of components report the stars they have drawn a few times a second, so the bar and its estimate follow them.

### Changed
- **A sliced component is drawn from streams of its own.** A slice draws from the component's stream with `:slice:` and its number added, with its share (1 over the slices) of the component's Poisson mean, so the slices together are a draw of the whole component and a seed gives the same stars at any worker count. A component that needs no slices keeps its stream and its stars; the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, the Sagittarius dwarf and any other component past the limit at the galaxy's floor draw different stars from before.
- **The plan of a scatter names its component tasks.** `component_key` of the shell scatter's and the phenomena's plans became `component_parts`, task by task the `[kind, name, slice, slices]` lists of the components it draws.
- **A scatter's log lines say which unit they are about and how big it is.** A line now reads `Bright stars, shells 100-131 (unit 12 of 512, about 1,200 stars expected): added ...`, and the components' and the phenomena's the same, so the sizes of the units can be read off the log.

## [8.0.1867] - 2026-10-22

**Headline:** The object index fills itself: the warm-up builds it, keeps it current and counts it against the cache budget.

### Changed
- **Object index builder (PERF.140).** `planetgen warm` has a new first family, `object-index` (the command `warm-object-index`), in the `opening` phase. It writes one `object_index` row for every system, star, planet, moon, belt, comet, facility and phenomenon, and a row changes only when what it holds changed. The first run builds each kind; later runs write only the objects edited since (a planet or moon edit reaches its row through its system), and remove the rows of objects that are gone. After `planetgen orbits` or a new generator epoch the index is built whole, since those move objects between sectors without touching the rows.
- **The index is kept first in the cache budget.** What the index takes on disk comes off `cache.max_mb` before the tile cache gets any of it.
- **`planetgen check-db object-index`.** Compares the index with the tables and says how many rows are missing, extra or different; it warns when nothing has built the index yet. It is not in the default list of checks.
- **The admin queue page** shows each kind's rows, when it last ran and the size of the index under the warm-up phases (`GET /api/admin/work/warm` gains `index`).

## [8.0.1866] - 2026-10-21

**Headline:** Every job queued to RQ now has a time limit taken from how long the system expects it to take, so a job whose worker was killed expires instead of staying on the queue for ever.

### Fixed
- **The Generate page's jobs, the API's jobs and the work queue's tasks were queued with no time limit (PERF.144).** Each one had `job_timeout=-1`, so RQ never expired the entry of a job whose worker died. Now every site gives a finite limit, ten times the best estimate, never under 15 minutes and never over its ceiling: a Generate page job from the recorded time of its steps (a floor of one hour, a ceiling of 30 days, which is also the limit of a job with a step that was never recorded), an API job from its route's estimate (the neighbourhood's `estimate.seconds`, a regeneration's recorded sector time, a slow page's expected seconds; seven days at most, and one hour for an edit nothing can estimate), a work queue task from its submitter's estimate or the recorded seconds of its kind (6 hours at most and when nothing is recorded), and the tile prefetch and rebuild from the size of the chunk. A units' limit is as before.
- **A Generate page job that RQ ends for its limit now stops its step.** The runner stops the step it was waiting on and reports the job failed with the reason, where the step used to run on.

### Changed
- **`redisqueue.queue` returns a `TimedQueue`.** It refuses a job queued with no limit, a limit of -1, zero or `None`, so a new kind of job cannot skip `redisqueue.job_timeout`; a test also fails on any `enqueue` call that does not name its limit and on any module that makes an RQ queue or job of its own. `units.UNIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `units.TIMEOUT_MULTIPLE` and `units.MIN_UNIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` are now `redisqueue.MAX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `TIMEOUT_MULTIPLE` and `MIN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`.

## [8.0.1863] - 2026-10-21

**Headline:** A run or job whose process was killed no longer blocks every new run or holds up an update, and `update.sh --reset-jobs` resets every job and the queue when something else is stuck.

### Fixed
- A run that owns the machine is the Redis key `planetgen:run:active`, which had no expiry and was freed only by the run's own process. A run killed with `kill -9`, by the out-of-memory killer or by a restart left it set, and every new run was refused as busy for ever. A run now records which process follows it and that process says it is alive at every poll (`runrecord.touch`); when a new run finds the machine held, it ends a run whose process is gone (same host: the process id is not running; another host, or a run recorded before this: no sign of life for two minutes) as failed, frees the machine and starts. The waiting units of the dead run do nothing.
- A queued job (a Generate page job, an API job) is queued with no time limit, so RQ never gave up the entry of one whose worker was killed: it stayed "running" in Redis, `update.sh` listed it, could not stop it, waited ten minutes and refused to update. The update guard and every worker now clear such jobs when they look (`workers.reap_dead_jobs`): a job whose worker is gone fails with a message saying so (or is queued again when it has a retry left), and a registry entry whose job has expired is dropped.

### Added
- `python3 -m planetgen.cli.reset_jobs` (`--yes`, `--dry-run`) resets every job and the queue: it stops what the update guard lists, kills the queue workers on the machine, removes the RQ keys and the run records in Redis (the admin's worker count and the caches stay) and the rows of the jobs table, frees and un-pauses the work lease, and prints what it found and removed.
- `sudo ./update.sh --reset-jobs` runs it first, without asking, before the guard is taken.

## [8.0.1862] - 2026-10-21

**Headline:** The site's caches are rebuilt by themselves after a generation run, an orbital update or an edit, without waiting for the next update.

### Changed
- **The warm-up starts after every change (PERF.141).** Anything that moves a data version tag (a generation run, `planetgen orbits`, an edit through the API, a change found in the galaxy) now asks for `planetgen warm`, which starts in the background as the web server's user, waits `cache.warm_settle_seconds` (default 60) so a burst of edits is one warm-up, and rebuilds only what the changes touched. A change that arrives during a run gets another round; nothing starts during an update (it warms at its end) or with `cache.warm_on_change` off (`PLANETGEN_WARM_ON_CHANGE=0`). Two new settings, `cache.warm_on_change` and `cache.warm_settle_seconds`.

**Headline:** The cache warm-up now runs in five named phases and says after each one what it built, what was already stored and what the cache budget left out.

### Changed
- **`planetgen warm` runs in phases (PERF.141).** In order: `opening` (the Galaxy Map's opening views and the first page of each list), `built-levels` (the tile octree's first levels), `deep-tiles` (the zoom run in to the centre), `objects` (the sector, system and phenomenon pages) and `search`. `warm-galaxy-tiles` is split in two for it, and the new `warm-galaxy-deep-tiles` command builds the zoom run. After each phase the run prints one line: `Phase 2 of 5, built-levels: 3 built, 125 already stored, 0 left out in 2.0 s.`, or `unchanged, nothing built` when the data under it has not changed since the last run, and `stopped at the cache budget` when `cache.max_mb` cut the tile phases short. A phase name can be given instead of families (`planetgen warm deep-tiles`).

## [8.0.1855] - 2026-10-21

**Headline:** The galaxy's disks are exponential in height, the form their scale heights are measured with, so a galaxy's midplane stars are twice as dense for the same mass.

### Changed
- **The thin and thick disks' vertical profile is `exp(-|z| / h)`, not the isothermal sheet `sech^2(z / 2h)`** (`galaxy/density.py` `_vertical`, `generation/object_first.py`, `galaxy/skeleton.py`, `html/static/galaxyprisms.js`). The scale heights the model uses (BHG16's 300 pc and 900 pc) are exponential fits to star counts; a `sech^2` sheet with the same tail has a column of `4 h` times its midplane density where the fit's is `2 h`, so for one stellar mass the midplane was half the fits' (GEN.404 made the density follow the mass and exposed it). The mass of each disk is unchanged (its column is `2 h` times the midplane now, `2 pi L^2 x 2 h` in `density._disk_mass`, `shape_draw.disk_masses` and `density.bulge_to_total`), so at the reference radius between two arms the density is 0.750 of the density the earlier calibration pinned there (it was 0.376 under GEN.404) and the column through that point is 524.26 pc of relative density before and after. The nuclear stellar disc keeps its `sech^2` height (`density._sech_vertical`).
  - The open clusters' heights (`generation/open_clusters.py`) and the neutron-star and black-hole height factor (`galaxy/remnant_distribution.py`) follow the stars' profile.
  - The reference galaxy's bulge amplitude is 3.11 / 2 (`mathcheck.REFERENCE_BULGE_AMPLITUDE`): BHG16's 3.11 was measured against the `sech^2` disk, and the bulge keeps its 31% of the mass.
  - `MAGNETAR_YOUNG_STAR_SHARE` is 0.0016 (it was 0.0019), the young population's share of the stars over the new profile.
  - The reference galaxy's outline reaches shell 3,596 (it was 3,147 under GEN.404, 3,762 before it); the rest of the gap to the pinned density is the mean system mass (GEN.545).
- The generator epoch is 41.

## [8.0.1853] - 2026-10-21

**Headline:** One setting, `cache.max_mb` (1 GB by default), sizes the stored caches, and when it is full the warm-up stops and only tiles nobody asked for lately are dropped.

### Changed
- **One cache size key, `cache.max_mb` (PERF.139).** It replaces `tile_cache.max_mb` and `PLANETGEN_TILE_CACHE_MAX_MB` with no compatibility shim (an old `tile_cache.max_mb` in `config.json` is ignored), defaults to 1024 MB instead of 200, and `0` turns the disk caches off. The Galaxy Map's tile cache is the first thing under it; the object index and the stored lists will share it. `update.sh`'s cache directory step and `docs/config.md` follow the new key.
- **What happens at the budget (PERF.133).** The tiles `planetgen warm`, the background build and the rebuild after a change build ahead are marked, and a visit sets the modification time of the file it reads. When the cache is over the budget `prune` deletes only the files a visit asked for, least recently visited first, down to 80%; a tile built ahead is never deleted for size. `planetgen warm` then stops building tiles and says how many it left out (`N tiles left out, the tile cache is full`).

## [8.0.1851] - 2026-10-21

**Headline:** A tile of the Galaxy Map is built again only when something it holds has changed, and a release alone no longer throws the stored tiles away.

### Changed
- **The stored tiles no longer follow the release number (PERF.133).** They are keyed by a new tile stamp (`db.query.galaxy_tile_stamp`, in `GET /api/galaxy/changes` as `tile_stamp` and `tile_full`) made of the galaxy shape, the bright-star seed, the naming key, a tile-format number (`db.query.TILE_FORMAT`) and the generator epoch, with the sector change counters. A release that changes neither the tile format nor the epoch keeps every stored tile, so the `planetgen warm` that `update.sh` starts after it finds them stored and builds none; the pages and counts cached by the old stamp are still dropped by a release. A change to what a tile holds or how it is packed raises `TILE_FORMAT`, and `tests/test_tile_format.py` fails until it does.
- **A change rebuilds what it touched at once.** When a sector is edited, added or given a system, only the tiles holding it (one per level) are deleted, and those that were stored are queued on the bulk queue for a rebuild straight away, coarsest first (at most 2,048 a change), so the next visit finds them built. It is off when `tile_cache.prefetch_per_minute` is 0, during an update and while the cache is full.

## [8.0.1850] - 2026-10-21

**Headline:** A neutron star's or stellar black hole's age now follows its population: the time since the star that made it collapsed.

### Changed
- `stellar_evolution.collapse_age_gy` draws a progenitor from the IMF over the kind's progenitor range, a birth age from the population's window and age law (as any star's), and returns the birth age less the time the progenitor took to collapse. Neutron stars and stellar black holes use it in place of an age uniform over 10 Gy; a young population's remnants are under 0.1 Gy old, a bulge's or halo's 8 to 13 Gy. The sector fill gives scattered rows, below-cut remnants, ejected remnants and rolled remnants their population as it gives a brown dwarf.

## [8.0.1849] - 2026-10-21

**Headline:** A white dwarf's planets are the ones that outlived its giant phase, moved outward by the mass the star lost.

### Added
- **White dwarf planets (GEN.318).** A white dwarf's planets are drawn as the ones that formed around its progenitor, then the giant phase removes everything inside the progenitor's engulfment radius, 1.5 AU for a solar-mass star and 0.8 AU more per solar mass above one, and the survivors' orbits widen by the star's mass before over its mass after (`a (M_star + M_planet)` is constant: 1.85 for a star of one solar mass that leaves 0.54). A white dwarf without a model progenitor (a forced type, a planetary nebula's central star) takes the mass that leaves it by the remnant relation, kept between 1 and 8 solar masses.
- **A planetary nebula's close pair holds a disk and no planets.** A close pair with a white dwarf as hot as a planetary nebula's central star (30,000 K or more) gets a circumbinary post-AGB disk on its primary (a mass between 0.01 and 0.1 solar masses, its inner edge the pair's stability limit, its outer edge 10 to 300 AU, with no bodies in it) and no planets. The star page names it.

### Changed
- The engulfment radius of a white dwarf was a fixed 1.5 AU for a population-model white dwarf and nothing for a forced type or a planetary nebula's central star; it now follows the progenitor's mass for every white dwarf, and a pair's post-common-envelope test reads it too.

## [8.0.1845] - 2026-10-21

**Headline:** The Galaxy Map's server now builds the tiles of the next few zoom steps, and the ones around a view, in the background while a visitor looks.

### Added
- **The tiles around a visit are built ahead of the visitor's next move (PERF.132).** When the map asks for tiles it now also sends where its camera and target are (`at`), and once the answer has gone the server queues, as low-priority jobs on the bulk queue, the tiles of the cut for the camera one to four fade bands closer along its line (the next zoom steps), then the neighbours of the requested tiles and the next level inside them (for a visitor who pans). A worker builds them into the same disk cache a request fills. It keeps to named limits, new settings of `tile_cache`: `prefetch_per_visit` (128 tiles a request), `prefetch_per_minute` (600) and `prefetch_max_queued` (8 jobs, 16 tiles each); it queues nothing for a tile already stored or already queued, nothing for ten minutes after the cache pruned itself, nothing during an update, and a malformed or missing `at` is ignored, so a visit to a built area queues nothing and a second visitor to the same area causes no build.
